historical_reviews.deepseek: The current read-only intent is relevant but not complete: a quoted range does not enumerate RTM0–RTM7 and the fallback is truncated. Duplicate-code data proves that code-only lookup can dangerously select fan-control operations.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly separates the passive RTM review from the critical fan-control variant. This review further requires a rear-transition/module physical definition and rejects fan RPM or PWM evidence as RTM temperature proof.
historical_reviews.duplicate_fan_variant: Row 1668 changes fan duty and requires physical removal/reinstall; its commands, 10/10-minute duration and recovery obligations are wholly outside this one-minute sensor-page row.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 requires each range member, ED-36 treats RTM meaning/topology and threshold tables as readiness inputs, and ED-38 protects thermal/log state and verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: Confirm that all applicable UBB RTM0–RTM7 temperature channels, once RTM is defined for this platform, identify the correct physical modules, present readable values and expose specification-correct thresholds in Dashboard and Server Health.
original_method: The platform owner defines RTM and enumerates its physical members, maps each module to an exact SDR record and both Web rows, supplies thermal limits and threshold masks, then automation collects complete passive per-member evidence for operator confirmation.
manual_activity: The board/platform owner defines RTM, maps each fitted RTM0–RTM7 component to a sensor and Web entry, provides expected readings and thresholds and reviews both Web views. No fan duty change, fan removal or link control belongs to this case.
required_inputs: Authoritative expansion of RTM for the target platform and physical RTM0–RTM7 topology
Fitted-module applicability, board/slot/connector identity and exact SDR record/entity per member
Temperature measurement location, units, scale, tolerance, freshness and unavailable semantics
Enabled threshold mask and expected lower/upper limit values
Operating/load/ambient context and any RTM link or board thermal relationship
BMC/SDR/RTM firmware versions and Dashboard/Server Health mapping
Secret-safe OOB collection, complete evidence retention and no-clear policy
Thermal/link aborts and independent BMC/platform recovery owner
safety_requirements: Match row 1851 and its variant, not the duplicate code alone
Never execute the duplicate row's fan-duty raw commands or physical fan procedure for this RTM check
Do not assume RTM meaning or reuse generic GPU/HSC sensor evidence
Enumerate exact RTM0–RTM7 records; a tilde label is not an executable range
Preserve full SDR and threshold access; do not cap evidence at 100 lines
Do not change thresholds, links, fans, power, BMC state or logs
Stop on missing/stale/invalid RTM sensor, threshold mismatch, thermal/link anomaly or BMC instability; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact row/variant and owner-defined RTM topology
Capture complete read-only SDR/Sensor inventory and exact member results
Parse per-member temperature, state, freshness and enabled thresholds
Build physical-module parity and prepare both Web rows for operator confirmation
Perform no fan control, physical action, link change, threshold write or verdict
engineer_actions: Define RTM and approve fitted module membership
Approve physical-to-SDR/Web mappings and thermal limits
Confirm both Web views and any unavailable-member treatment
Review each RTM channel and issue the overall result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The current-row `sensor get` idea is passive, but the literal range and truncated fallback are incomplete. Code-only selection can instead expose row 1668's conflicting raw fan commands; those must never run here.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Using the exact row identity and secret-safe OOB access, retain the full SDR inventory and query each owner-mapped RTM sensor individually, including threshold flags, then compare with its Dashboard and Server Health entries.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: RTM0~7 scope, two BMC-Web paths, human-readable reading/threshold criterion and 1/1-minute estimates are preserved; the duplicate fan procedure and 10/10 minutes are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES RTM SEMANTIC/TOPOLOGY AND THRESHOLD PACKAGE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Publish an RTM physical map, enumerate only its fitted records, collect full passive sensor evidence and normalize enabled thresholds before a two-view Web comparison.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Protects row identity against a hazardous duplicate-code collision and converts the range label into module-specific evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A literal name, generic SDR excerpt, fan RPM or fan-duty response cannot demonstrate RTM0–RTM7 temperatures and programmed thresholds.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Readback is non-destructive, but wrong RTM semantics or duplicate-row selection can either mask board overheating or trigger dangerous cooling changes.

project_override_considerations: If RTM denotes rear transition modules or another vendor-specific component, the approved platform specification must state that meaning and per-index placement. Unfitted indices require explicit not-applicable status rather than silent omission.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and two-code-variant separation audit
Approved RTM definition and physical RTM0–RTM7 topology/applicability
Reading location, units, state, freshness and enabled-threshold table
Complete redacted SDR and exact sensor results with status/timestamps
Dashboard and Server Health screenshots/exports per mapped member

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Within row 1851, Items, Web procedure and criteria consistently describe RTM sensor readings and thresholds. The duplicate-code fan case is a separate atomic row, not an internal contradiction in this variant.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A distinct passive RTM sensor-family check is identifiable. RTM semantics, fitted topology and threshold values are owner-supplied readiness inputs under ED-36; execution remains gated until supplied.

review_improvement: Quarantines a critical fan-control duplicate, requires an owner-defined physical RTM map and prevents literal-range, truncated or fan evidence from satisfying this passive thermal row.
independent_technical_reasoning: This duplicated code spans two radically different blast radii: one row actively overrides cooling and removes a fan, while this row reads RTM temperatures. Source row and variant ID therefore outrank code identity. For the current row, the remaining engineering problem is semantic and topological attribution of RTM0–RTM7, which can be solved by a versioned board map and passive per-record evidence without borrowing any fan-control behavior.
